solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nervous diner perhaps making a mess of meal's cod

indicators.note: to make a mess of something is to jumble it up, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A jittery restaurant customer botches a plate of cod.
explanation.walkthrough: Damocles was the courtier seated at a banquet beneath a sword hung by a single hair, so he is a diner with every reason to be nervous; 'perhaps' flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: In the classical story the courtier dined under a dangling sword, the archetype of anxious feasting.

clue.text: Split personality's first attacked with tear gas — the wrong way!

indicators.note: going the wrong way means running backwards, so everything is read in reverse
first takes the opening letter of personality's

parts.note: Mace is a brand of tear gas spray, so maced means sprayed with it

explanation.surface: A multiple personality is gassed in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split personality' looks like one phrase, but 'Split' is the definition, meaning leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To split is slang for leaving in a hurry, and to decamp is to depart suddenly.

clue.text: One's venomous combination of arts and business qualifications

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts degree
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration degree

explanation.surface: A poisonous person holding a mix of arts and business degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's venomous' means 'this one is venomous', defining the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a deadly African snake, a prime example of a venomous creature.

clue.text: Deafening boom's beginning in damned storm

indicators.note: in puts these pieces within the damned word

parts.note: curst is an old spelling of cursed, meaning damned
something deafening is extremely loud

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A deafening thunderclap starts up in a dreadful storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curst' is an archaic spelling of 'cursed', a word solvers may not expect to meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudburst is a sudden, violent downpour of rain, a type of storm.

clue.text: Endless bickering where health benefits are offered

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel or bickering

explanation.surface: Constant squabbling at a place meant for wellbeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a resort with mineral springs or treatments taken for one's health.

clue.text: Crime writer, far from sinister?

definitions.meaning: Colin ... wrote the Inspector Morse detective novels
in heraldry sinister is the left side and its opposite, the right side, has the Latin-derived name meaning right-handed

explanation.surface: A detective novelist who is anything but menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' reads as menacing, but in heraldry it simply means left; the question mark admits the wordplay on the opposite side.
explanation.definitionFit: Colin Dexter is the novelist behind Inspector Morse, and dexter is the heraldic term for the right side, the opposite of sinister.

clue.text: Other part involved when getting one's leg over

indicators.note: turned over, the selected letters are read backwards
only part of the phrase is used, the letters involved within it

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about another party being involved in a sexual encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting one's leg over' is British slang for having sex; here 'over' reverses the letters taken from inside 'one's leg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Else means other or different, as in someone else.

clue.text: Youth having jelly with daughter in outdoor restaurant

indicators.note: having means holding, so the youth contains the next pieces

parts.note: a teen is a young person
agar is a jelly made from seaweed

explanation.surface: A teenager eats jelly with their daughter at an open-air café.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an open-air café or garden where refreshments are served.

clue.text: Something to secure sails oftener crumpled across end of deck

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the rearranged letters lie on both sides of the next piece
crumpled means crushed out of shape, so these letters are rearranged
the end of the word deck is its last letter

explanation.surface: Sails crumple more often across the end of a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' makes REEFNOT from 'oftener', which goes 'across' K.
explanation.definitionFit: The reef knot is the classic sailor's knot used to tie in reefs, securing the furled part of a sail.

clue.text: Band's attempt to hide shiny dome, more than half finished

indicators.note: five of the eight letters are kept and the closing stretch is dropped, so the word is cut short past its halfway point

parts.note: a comb-over is hair swept across a bald scalp to disguise it

explanation.surface: A musician's group tries to conceal a bald head, but the job is only partly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than half finished' removes VER, leaving five of the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small group of jazz or dance musicians, so it is a kind of band.

clue.text: Baronet stashing odd cask to mature out of public view

indicators.note: to stash is to hide something away, so the baronet's letters hold the next piece inside them
odd means strange or irregular, telling us the letters of cask come out rearranged

parts.note: to age is to mature or grow older

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman hides a strange barrel of wine to let it mature where no one sees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' looks like it describes the cask, but it is the anagram signal, and the rearranged letters sit inside the baronet's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstage describes what happens behind the scenes, hidden from the audience or public.

clue.text: Earthy tone isn't unusual in upsetting old queen with problem

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the turned pieces
in a down clue, upsetting turns the pieces upside down, reading them from the bottom

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain in the early 1700s
a rub is a difficulty, as in there's the rub

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: An unusual colour comes from troubling a former monarch with a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns ANNE RUB into BURENNA; 'unusual' turns ISNT into NTSI, which goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt sienna is a reddish-brown pigment made from roasted earth, a classic earth colour.

clue.text: To salvage parts from wreck is in balance

indicators.note: to wreck something is to smash it apart, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Salvaging parts from a wreck is a delicate balancing act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreck' looks like a noun after 'from', but 'from' belongs to the definition and 'wreck' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cannibalise a machine is to strip it for usable components to repair others.

clue.text: Cruel, heartless mocking, full of twists and turns

parts.note: mean can mean unkind or cruel

indicators.note: losing the heart means the central letters of the word are removed

parts.note: deriding is mocking or ridiculing

explanation.surface: Someone's unkind, unfeeling ridicule goes all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle ID out of DERIDING, leaving DERING.
explanation.definitionFit: A meandering path or river winds back and forth, full of bends and turns.

clue.text: Question mark appears at left of screen

indicators.note: the mark's letter is placed before, on the left of, the other piece

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A question mark pops up on the left side of a computer screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Question mark' looks like one punctuation sign, but it splits into a verb and an abbreviation; 'screen' is a verb-or-noun meaning cover, not a monitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A mask is something that screens or hides a face, and to mask is to screen.

clue.text: Female member of clergy losing the lead on Spanish cape

indicators.note: losing the lead means dropping the first letter

parts.note: a minister is a member of the clergy
re means on or concerning, as in letters re a matter

explanation.surface: A woman cleric loses her leadership role on a headland in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Finisterre is a headland in Galicia on the north-west coast of Spain.

clue.text: Provincial company not put to the test about uncertainty

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the untested word goes round the uncertainty

parts.note: untried means never tested
an if is a doubt or uncertainty, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A rural firm, never tested, wavers over its doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: IF as a noun, a doubt or condition, is the convention here.
explanation.definitionFit: Countrified describes rustic, unsophisticated manners, which is what provincial means as an adjective.

clue.text: Person arriving to protect stronghold, one that brings relief

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so the arriving person's letters go around the next piece

parts.note: a comer is one who comes or arrives
a fort is a fortified stronghold

explanation.surface: A newcomer arrives to defend a fortress and bring relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A comforter is someone or something that consoles and eases distress.

clue.text: Rotation of planetary sphere is relative

indicators.note: rotating something half a turn here means reading the word from the other end

parts.note: an orb is a sphere, especially a heavenly body

explanation.surface: A planet's spin is a matter of perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotation' looks like astronomy, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bro is informal shorthand for brother, a family member or relative.

clue.text: Union's base turned smaller during brief skirmish

indicators.note: during places the turned piece inside the shortened skirmish
brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a brush is a brief encounter or skirmish, as in a brush with the law

indicators.note: turned means reversed, read backwards

parts.note: less means smaller

explanation.surface: A union's base shrinks during a short dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' is the European Union, not a trade union; 'turned' makes SSEL from LESS, which goes into BRUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Brussels is the seat of the main institutions of the European Union.

clue.text: Wife and husband go off source of gluten to tolerate in diet

indicators.note: to go off is to depart, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: wheat is the grain from which gluten mostly comes

explanation.surface: A married couple gives up wheat to cope with a gluten-free diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' reads as going off a food, but it removes W and H from WHEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be able to eat something is to tolerate it as part of one's diet.

clue.text: Working with teeth initially meshed, one side of cog breaking a channel

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word meshed
breaking means interrupting, so the other pieces split the channel apart

parts.note: a station is a broadcasting channel
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: one side of the word cog is its edge letter, here the first

explanation.surface: Gear teeth mesh, and a broken cog wrecks a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working with teeth' suggests machinery and gears; it means chewing food.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastication is chewing, the process of breaking food down with the teeth.

clue.text: Make good theatre company put on show

indicators.note: in a down clue the company is put on top of, placed above, the show

parts.note: a rep is a repertory theatre company
to air is to show or broadcast

explanation.surface: A theatre company stages a production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on show' reads as staging a play, but 'put on' places REP above AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair is to fix or restore, which is to make something good again.

clue.text: Lighter spades are daunting

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
to cow is to intimidate or daunt

explanation.surface: Light spades are intimidating to someone digging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' is not a comparative but a noun: a flat barge used to unload ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat used as a lighter for carrying goods to and from ships.

clue.text: Marching one abreast, crossing middle of hostile desert, enter secretly

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the marching phrase goes around the next pieces

parts.note: soldiers marching in file go one behind another, a single person across the line

indicators.note: the centre letter of the word hostile is taken

parts.note: to rat is to desert or abandon one's side

explanation.surface: Troops in single file cross hostile desert to slip in unseen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like sand, but it is the verb to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To infiltrate is to slip into an organisation or territory covertly.

clue.text: Stir pint to make one's own

parts.note: a stir is a fuss or commotion, an ado

explanation.surface: Stir a pint to give it your own touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt something is to take it up and claim it as yours.

clue.text: Give up length cut from duvet

indicators.note: cut from means removed from the word that follows

parts.note: a quilt is a padded bed cover, like a duvet

explanation.surface: Abandon a duvet that has been cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to stop or abandon something, which is to give it up.

clue.text: Support needs time for introduction of care attendants

indicators.note: one letter standing for another means it replaces it

parts.note: to encourage is to give support

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A support scheme needs time before care attendants can be introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps T in for C, the first letter of 'care'.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants or followers who accompany an important person.

clue.text: Starts to give you muscles? It might

definitions.text: Starts to give you muscles? It might

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of each following word

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a fitness place might build up your muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the place that might give you muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym is a fitness centre where workouts build up strength and muscle.

clue.text: Short glass of beer after port wine

indicators.note: the beer piece comes after the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major port, often shortened to Rio

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: A quick half of beer followed by a glass of port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'a jar' is a pint at the pub. 'port' looks like the fortified wine, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Spanish region of La Rioja.

clue.text: Delivery from a Mister Right, bitten by a dog

indicators.note: being bitten means being held in the jaws, so the dog's letters close round this one

parts.note: a spitz is a breed of dog with a pointed muzzle

explanation.surface: Mr Right, the perfect partner, gets bitten by a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister Right' reads as a romantic ideal, but 'a Mister' is a spray device and 'Right' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritz is a short squirt of liquid, just what a spray atomiser delivers.

clue.text: Less conceited person associated with fashion?

parts.note: mode means fashion or style
the suffix -ster forms nouns for someone linked to a thing, as in gangster or prankster

explanation.surface: A question about whether a fashion person is more humble.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the answer looks like a noun for a fashion person; it is in fact the comparative of a common adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Modester is the comparative of modest, meaning more humble and less vain.
